question: What do rho.negation, rho.plain and bsgs.negation cost, as sealed ecbench bounds with the section 5a band, on generic prime-order curves at log2 r 32-49 (the medium tier), and is the toy excess of rho.negation over sqrt(pi/4) finite-size set-up or a persistent walk shortfall?

claims.text: Every admitted run recovers the planted logarithm and every run replays exactly (pod verify --replay-all and a local re-audit).

The medium-tier bound constant of rho.negation (ratio to the floor sqrt(pi/4), w = 0) is classified by the PROTOCOL.md section 9 table: setup_excess, walk_shortfall, intermediate_excess or unresolved.
claims.if_supported: seal docs/bounds/records/prime-medium-rho-neg*.json; report the toy/medium factor as derived; update the lead
claims.if_not_supported: report the verdict as written; walk_shortfall reopens LEAD-RHO-negation-map-fruitless-cycles

claims.text: The harness resolves a known sqrt(2) constant (rho.plain over rho.negation) at medium sizes.
The finite-size law R(N) = 1 + c N^-beta (and R_inf + c N^-beta) fitted over toy and medium sizes, N = sqrt(r).
Nothing here is a statement about cryptographic sizes or a lower bound on ECDLP.

hypotheses.statement: The toy excess of rho.negation is set-up: the medium-tier constant is within 1.10 x the floor.
hypotheses.mechanism: O(log r) jump-table and start set-up plus distinguished-point overshoot are a vanishing fraction of sqrt(r); an r-adding walk adds only a few percent

seed_derivation.note: seeds.json: seed(tag) = int(SHA-256('prime_medium_tier_rho_20261107/v1/' + tag)[0:12 hex], 16) for curve, target and measurement seeds, written before any data; ecbench derives per-run algorithm seeds from them

power.note: cluster bootstrap over workloads (ecbench bound fit). primary decision is one interval (rho.negation medium constant). Per-run SD about 0.55 x floor (prior pool) gives SE about 0.025 over 480 runs per arm; 96 runs per size and arm (>= 24 required). Secondary tests: Holm over 3 methods and over 5 curve-effect tests.

stopping_rules.rule: six jobs (J1-J6), each once; fixed N
a per-execution timeout (300 s) or exhaustion is a censored row kept in the session

an incomplete session (Spot loss, launcher failure) is kept and rerun once under a new job name with the identical spec; a second failure stops that job and the bound is fitted on the completed sessions, saying so
a complete session with a passing audit is admitted for counts even if the pod's L2 gate failed; its wall time is not reported

decision_rule.text: PROTOCOL.md section 9. M = medium constant.ratio_to_floor of rho.negation at w = 0. setup_excess if M <= 1.10 and ci95_hi < 1.30; walk_shortfall if M >= 1.30 and ci95_lo > 1.10; intermediate_excess if ci95_lo > 1.10 and M < 1.30; unresolved otherwise; within_1.10_strict reported when ci95_hi <= 1.10; inconclusive if the positive control (plain/neg interval lower end above 1.2) fails or any audit fails. Correction: the primary is a single interval (no correction); Holm applies to the secondary families (three method constants; five curve-effect tests).
decision_rule.statistic: bound constant ratio_to_floor (mean over sizes of mean S / floor)
decision_rule.interval: ecbench cluster bootstrap 95%, 2000 resamples, harness seed

graphs: ratio to floor against log2 r, toy and medium, with model A and B

inadmissible: changing curves, seeds, targets, rounds, arms, unit, accounting, weights or thresholds after any result
pooling toy and medium in one bound
reading the R(N) extrapolation beyond 49 bits as a measurement
quoting local or non-L2 wall time
rerunning a complete session because of its numbers
